question: Lithostratigraphic classification (formal lithostratigraphic codes and hierarchy) was initially advanced in:
notes: Formal lithostratigraphic classification was pioneered and standardized in the United States by the American Commission on Stratigraphic Nomenclature (ACSN, later NACSN).

question: The Devonian formations were first described and established from:
notes: The Devonian System was erected in 1839 by Sir Roderick Murchison and Adam Sedgwick based on the marine strata of Devonshire (Devon), southwest England.

question: Which of the following stratigraphic systems was established later than the other three in the Lower Paleozoic group?
notes: Charles Lapworth established the Ordovician System in 1879 to resolve the fierce controversy between Murchison (Silurian) and Sedgwick (Cambrian) over overlapping strata in Wales.

question: The stages Georgian, Acadian and Potsdamian belong to which of the following systems?
notes: In North American chronostratigraphy, the Lower, Middle, and Upper Cambrian series were classically designated as the Georgian (Waucoban), Acadian, and Potsdamian (Croixian) stages.

question: In classical Cenozoic stratigraphy, the Neogene period includes:
notes: Historically in European stratigraphy, the Neogene included the Oligocene, Miocene, and Pliocene (or Miocene and Pliocene in modern ICS usage; option c represents the classic textbook division).

question: The transitional formations between the Upper Cretaceous and Palaeocene known as the 'Passage beds' are represented worldwide by the:
notes: The Danian stage (named by Desor, 1847 from Stevns Klint, Denmark) represents the earliest Paleocene marine sequence immediately succeeding the Maastrichtian K-Pg boundary event.

question: 'Permian' is named after 'Perm', a historical province in:
notes: Sir Roderick Murchison named the Permian System in 1841 after the extensive Perm province in the Ural Mountains region of Russia.

question: The type locality and original naming region for the Triassic System is:
notes: Friedrich von Alberti coined the name 'Trias' in 1834 for the classic three-part succession (Bunter sandstone, Muschelkalk limestone, and Keuper marls) of central Germany.

question: All branches of stratigraphy (litho-, bio-, chrono-, and sequence stratigraphy) are fundamentally based on:
notes: Stratigraphy is fundamentally an observational field science rooted in the mapping, measuring, and physical tracing of layered rocks in the field.

question: The first fundamental generalization and cornerstone law of stratigraphy is the:
notes: Formulated by Nicolas Steno in 1669, the Law of Superposition dictates that in an undeformed sedimentary sequence, older beds lie at the bottom and progressively younger beds succeed above.

question: If sedimentary deposition takes place inside a subterranean limestone cavern or cave:

options.a: It follows the law of superposition strictly
options.b: It does not follow the law of superposition
options.c: It may or may not follow the law of superposition

notes: Cave sedimentation (speleothems, cave collapse breccias, underground stream fills) violates standard superposition because younger sediments are deposited below older cavern roof rocks.

question: Which of the following serves as a reliable tectonic criterion for determining stratigraphic superposition and way-up in deformed terrains?
notes: Cleavage-bedding angular relationships serve as structural/tectonic criteria: when cleavage dips steeper than bedding, beds are right-way-up; when bedding dips steeper than cleavage, beds are overturned.

question: Which of the following represents the strongest primary sedimentary criterion for determining stratigraphic younging and superposition?
notes: Normal graded bedding (coarse grains at the base fining upward to silt/clay deposited by turbidity currents) provides an unambiguous primary physical indicator of depositional facing.

question: The regional correlation of unfossiliferous Precambrian terranes is primarily based on:
notes: Due to the absence of diagnostic macrofossils, Precambrian cratonic correlations rely on lithological sequences, unconformities, tectonothermal events, and high-precision isotopic geochronology.

question: Which of the following lithological units has been widely utilized as an isochronous key bed for precise inter-basinal correlation?
notes: Bentonite beds (smectite-rich devitrified volcanic ash falls) represent geologically instantaneous events deposited over hundreds of thousands of square kilometers, forming perfect isochronous marker beds.

question: According to William Smith's LAW OF FAUNAL SUCCESSION:

options.a: The fossil content of each formation is non-diagnostic
options.b: The fossil assemblage of each formation is the same as that of overlying and underlying beds
options.c: The fossil assemblage of each formation is distinctive and characteristically distinct
options.d: The fossils in a formation are arranged successively according to their physical size

notes: Formulated by William Smith (1799, 1815), the Law of Faunal Succession states that sedimentary strata contain distinctive fossil assemblages that succeed one another in a definite, predictable order.

question:
The chief characteristics of a superior index (zone) fossil are:
(1) Presence of complicated morphological structures
(2) Presence of simple structures
(3) Ability to float or swim (pelagic/planktic dispersal)
(4) Tendency to remain stationary or attached (sessile benthic)
notes: In Dr. Ausaf Sayeed's text key, option a is designated; note that in modern paleontology, complicated morphology (1) and wide pelagic dispersal (3) characterize ideal index fossils (e.g., ammonites and graptolites).

question: A death assemblage of fossil organisms accumulated and buried together in a sedimentary deposit is scientifically termed a:
notes: Coined by Wasmund (1926), a thanatocoenose is a death assemblage composed of skeletal remains brought together post-mortem by sedimentary transport or localized mortality.

question: A living community of interrelated, mutually interacting organisms inhabiting a defined geographical area is described as a:
notes: Coined by Karl Möbius (1877), a biocenose (biocoenosis) describes an interactive ecological life community occupying a biotope under natural environmental equilibrium.

question: The formal concept and terminology of 'biostratigraphy' was introduced into geological science by:
notes: Sydney Savory Buckman (1893, 1902) systematically introduced biostratigraphic terminology, refining biozones and epiboles through his ammonite studies.

question: A biostratigraphic zone consisting of the strata deposited during the maximum abundance (climax or acme) of an organism is called an:
notes: An epibole (termed by Trueman, 1923; equivalent to Acme Zone or Abundance Zone) represents the stratal body deposited during the acme or maximum numerical development of a taxon.

question: A biostratigraphic unit consisting of all the strata deposited during the total geological existence (stratigraphic range) of a zonal taxon is called a:
notes: A Taxon-Range Biozone comprises the body of strata representing the total horizontal and vertical range of occurrence of specimens of a particular taxon.

question: Who is universally recognized in geological literature as the 'Father of Historical Geology and English Stratigraphy'?
notes: In Dr. Ausaf Sayeed's text key, option b is recorded; William Smith is classically honored as the 'Father of English Stratigraphy' and Charles Lyell as the author of 'Principles of Geology'.

question: The first geologist in history to measure and publish actual detailed vertical stratigraphic sections of stratified rocks was:
notes: Johann Gottlob Lehmann (1756) recorded the first detailed stratigraphic cross-sections in the Harz Mountains of Germany, dividing rocks into Primitive, Secondary, and Alluvial orders.

question: The greatest modern advance in global stratigraphic correlation by means of worldwide Eustatic sea-level fluctuations was made by:
notes: Austrian geologist Eduard Suess coined the term 'Eustasy' in 1888 in 'Das Antlitz der Erde', proving that simultaneous transgressions and regressions across continents reflect global changes in sea level.

question: The historical geological concept of Abraham Gottlob Werner postulating that all crustal rocks precipitated sequentially from a universal primeval ocean is called:
notes: Neptunism (promoted by Werner in the late 18th century at Freiberg) asserted that all rocks—including basalt and granite—precipitated out of a receding universal primordial ocean.

question: Mappable, recognizable bodies of stratified rocks defined and distinguished solely by their lithological characteristics are called:
notes: Lithostratigraphic units (Rock units: Formation, Group, Member, Bed) are defined strictly on observable physical lithic properties without regard to geologic time.

question: Which of the following is NOT a chronostratigraphic (time-rock) unit?
notes: Epoch is a geochronologic (pure time) unit corresponding to the chronostratigraphic (time-rock) unit 'Series'. System, Series, and Stage are time-rock units.

question: Which of the following represents the principal and highest-ranking formal unit of geologic time?
notes: An Eon is the highest formal category of geologic time (e.g., Hadean, Archean, Proterozoic, Phanerozoic), encompassing multiple Eras.

question: Geological time is majorly divided at the base of the Cambrian Period into two grand divisions termed:
notes: The Precambrian (Cryptozoic Eon) comprises ~88% of Earth history, terminating at 538.8 Ma where the fossiliferous Phanerozoic Eon begins.

question: Which of the following serves as the fundamental, primary mapping unit in lithostratigraphic classification?
notes: The Formation is the fundamental unit of lithostratigraphy, possessing lithological homogeneity and mappability at normal field scales (typically 1:24,000 to 1:50,000).

question: In stratigraphic definition, the formal term 'Formation' denotes uniformity or similarity of:
notes: A formation reflects consistent lithologic character, coherent sedimentary genesis/facies architecture, and defined depositional interval.

question: Lens-shaped, laterally pinching-out lithologically distinct subordinate rock units within a formation are termed:
notes: In stratigraphic codes, lentils and tongues are formal subordinate members: lentils are laterally discontinuous lens-shaped bodies pinching out in all directions.

question: The chronostratigraphic (time-rock) unit 'Stage' corresponds directly with which formal geochronologic (time) unit?
notes: Standard stratigraphic equivalence: Erathem = Era; System = Period; Series = Epoch; Stage = Age; Chronozone = Chron.

question: A 'Biozone' is formally defined as a:
notes: A biozone is the fundamental formal unit of biostratigraphy, defined exclusively by its fossil content and taxon associations independently of lithology or time boundaries.

question:
Match the following chronostratigraphic units with their corresponding geochronologic time equivalents:
A. Erathem (Group) — 1. Epoch
B. System — 2. Age
C. Series — 3. Era
D. Stage — 4. Period
notes: Erathem corresponds to Era (A-3), System corresponds to Period (B-4), Series corresponds to Epoch (C-1), and Stage corresponds to Age (D-2).

question: In international stratigraphic nomenclature, which formal unit typically consists of only two words (a geographic name followed by the rank term)?
notes: Formal subordinate stratigraphic units such as Members (e.g., 'Semri Member') or formations consist of a geographic place name followed by the lithologic or rank designator.

question: Which of the following geological intervals has been historically designated as the 'Psychozoic' era (Age of Human Mind)?
notes: Coined by Joseph LeConte (1877), the Psychozoic Era designates the Quaternary Period, characterized by the emergence, global expansion, and cultural ascendancy of humans.

question: The Cryptozoic Eon (Precambrian) is etymologically and scientifically designated as:
notes: Cryptozoic derives from Greek 'kryptos' (hidden) and 'zoon' (life), contrasting with Phanerozoic ('phaneros' = visible/evident life).

question: The earliest definitive macro-fossil evidence of upright, vascular land plants (e.g., Cooksonia) appears in the:
notes: Vascular land plants first appear as megafossils (Cooksonia) in the Mid-to-Late Silurian (Wenlock-Ludlow), following microfossil cryptospores from the Ordovician.

question: Amphibians (the earliest tetrapods, such as Ichthyostega and Acanthostega) originated during the:
notes: The water-to-land vertebrate transition occurred during the Late Devonian (Frasnian-Famennian), with lobe-finned sarcopterygian fish evolving into stem tetrapods.

question: First widespread angiosperms (flowering plants) bearing true leaves and floral structures originated and diversified during the:
notes: Angiosperms arose in the Early Cretaceous and experienced explosive adaptive radiation during the Late Cretaceous, restructuring terrestrial ecosystems.

question: The major paroxysmal orogenic phase and peak uplift of the European Alps Mountains occurred during the:
notes: While Alpine subduction began in the Mesozoic, the climax of collision between Africa and Europe producing vast nappe stacking and major surface uplift occurred in the Miocene.

question: Which of the following geological periods is famously designated in historical geology as the 'Age of Cycads'?
notes: The Jurassic Period is celebrated as the 'Age of Cycads' (and Bennettitales), which constituted up to 70% of the world's terrestrial flora alongside gymnosperm conifers and ferns.

question: The Mesozoic Era commenced approximately how many millions of years ago (Ma)?
notes: The Mesozoic Era began at 251.9 Ma following the Permian-Triassic mass extinction, enduring for approximately 186 million years until the K-Pg boundary (66 Ma).

question: The most widely utilized and foundational acoustic data in seismic stratigraphy consists of:
notes: Conventional reflection seismic surveys record compressional P-wave reflections generated at acoustic impedance contrasts (velocity x density) across stratal bedding surfaces.

question: The simplest, most objective, and most fundamental of all biostratigraphic units is the:
notes: A range zone (taxon-range zone) represents the simplest and most empirically verifiable biostratigraphic unit, defined solely by the lowest and highest stratigraphic occurrences of a single taxon.

question: Choose the correct formal hierarchical combination of pure geochronologic time units from largest to smallest:
notes: The formal geochronologic hierarchy defined by the International Commission on Stratigraphy is: Eon -> Era -> Period -> Epoch -> Age -> Chron.

question: Which of the following is the oldest magnetic polarity epoch in the Late Cenozoic geomagnetic polarity time scale (GPTS)?
notes: In the standard GPTS: Gilbert reversed (~5.33–3.58 Ma) is the oldest, followed by Gauss normal (~3.58–2.58 Ma), Matuyama reversed (~2.58–0.78 Ma), and Brunhes normal (0.78 Ma to present).

question: Which of the following represents the correct chronological sequence of the major divisions of the Indian Geological Time Scale from oldest to youngest?
notes: Sir Thomas Holland (1906) classified Indian stratigraphy into four grand divisions: Archaean (crystalline basement), Purana (unmetamorphosed Proterozoic), Dravidian (Cambrian-Carboniferous marine), and Aryan (Upper Carboniferous to Recent).
